chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Maymoun, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The sustenance is quicker to the one who feeds the food than the knife in the hump (of a camel).
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of feeding others according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet (peace be upon him) uses the vivid metaphor of a knife sliding effortlessly into a camel's hump to illustrate how quickly divine sustenance (rizq) follows the act of feeding others. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on voluntary charity (sadaqah) not merely as a moral duty, but as a spiritual mechanism that removes obstacles to wealth and accelerates blessings. It reflects the broader theological principle that generosity opens the gates of provision, linking material ease directly to one's generosity toward creation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah Bin Maymoun, 
(It has been narrated) from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘
The sustenance is quicker to the one who feeds the food than the knife in the hump (of a camel)’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Faddal from ‘Abd Allah ibn Maymun who has said the following: “Ja’far from his father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has narrated that the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
Sustenance comes to a man, who serves food, faster than a knife goes into the hump on the back of a camel.’”
